item.title: Mini Essay - 'Surely You're Joking Mr Feynman' (Richard Feynman)
item.description:
During your walk this morning you finished “Surely Your Joking Mr Feynman”, and it’s been an interesting audiobook to listen to.

When I first started it, I was utterly convinced that it was absolutely brilliant - that Feynman was really connecting with that passion for the universe that I crave, that he had plenty of character and quirks that made him an engaging personality who genuinely loved learning about the universe. I’m sure that’s all true, but the further into the book I got the less I liked him - the whole thing started to feel like a collection of little stories from his life that didn’t build or develop into anything. Just snippets of experience and fun “cocktail event” type stories.

item.title: Mini Essay - 15000 days
item.description: On Friday I hit the 15,000 day mark - 15,000 days that I’ve been alive and living on this planet. It’s strange to think that I started tracking my days alive when I first discovered Mars One, and stranger still to discover that I hadn’t created a markdown file for Mars One until just now. It still feels like it’s a thing that I’m trying to forget or let go, and yet it was one of the things that lit me up the most in the world. I think the hurt I experienced with Mars One and the criticism it (and I in turn) received really left a major mark on my psyche, and in many ways I’m really just recovering from it and finding my feet again all these years after the program officially shutdown. I love that I track my days on Earth, and especially enjoyed that I might one day be able to countdown the number of days I’d have left - not because I was dying, but because I was leaving for another world. Seeing my time on Earth as being finite and measurable provided an enormous sense of purpose - that days are never to be wasted, and that I am capable of doing so very much with what I have that each day on Earth is an opportunity to make things better for myself and for others.

item.title: Mini Essay - Appeal of a dark, empty forest outpost
item.description:
For years now there’s been something drawing you to the quiet darkness of an otherwise empty forest outpost. There are critical elements to this interest though which are non-negotiable - it they’re not present, then the entire vibe is thrown off and it doesn’t work.

First and foremost is rain sounds. You knew the moment you heard the sounds of rain as the ship passed Saturn in Interstellar that it’s the sound that relaxes you most - the sounds that drowns out the other noise, any intrusive thoughts you might have, and never distracts you in itself. Right now you’ve got the Dark Forest Ambient Focus Music from YouTube on the other screen as you type, and the ambient synths are a fraction distracting… but the rain sounds that run underneath help make up for it.

item.title: Mini Essay - Appeal of living out of a van
item.description: One of the ideas that has stuck with me for decades now is the idea of living alone out of a van. I had the opportunity to do it when I went to Iceland in 2016, and it’s always stuck with me as a wonderful but slightly dislocated existence - like I knew I enjoyed having everything in my car and being free to go anywhere at any time, but not feeling like I could really stop anywhere either.

item.title: Mini Essay - Appeal of Small
item.description:
There’s something uniquely engaging about the world of the small. Whether it’s plastic WH40k miniatures, bonsai trees, LEGO, tilt-shift photography, ant colonies, model railways, or any one of a dozen other examples, there’s something that hooks the attention of many people in a way that the full scale version doesn’t.

Part of me thinks this may be a predominantly masculine trait, especially when I think things like toy soldiers and action figures, but then I only need to think of Barbie and Polly Pocket to realise that this particular focus on the world of the small isn’t really gendered - it’s just that we more often see men with hobbies that lend themselves to small things.

item.title: Mini Essay - Appeal of Thronglets
item.description: For some time I’ve wanted to rewatch the “Plaything” episode of Black Mirror with the express intent of zeroing in on why there’s so much appeal in an evolving digital sentience. On the surface the thronglets are terrifying - a digital lifeform that might be initially dismissed as an addictive game that’s hooked a vulnerable and emotionally overwhelmed man who took acid and became convinced the thronglets were talking to him, but they’re revealed at the end to be exactly as powerful and intelligent as he claimed when an audio signal rewrites the brains of everyone who hears it.

item.title: Mini Essay - April 19 (2023)
item.description:
Mini Essay - April 19 (2026)

I want to preface this by saying I wasn’t expecting to write it, and I’ve been working for the last few days on an entirely different and unrelated post about how I’m preparing for Mars One selection later this year. I’ll still publish that post in the next few days, but I’m not sure if I’ll publish this outside of Patreon. Maybe next year. Truth be told I may not publish this at all – all I know is I just realised what the date is, it stopped me in my tracks, and I need to write this right down while I’m feeling what I’m feeling.

item.title: Mini Essay - April 19 (2026)
item.description:
Mini Essay - April 19 (2023)

Having just re-read Mini Essay - April 19 (2023) I realise that I don’t really know how to describe the way I feel about it anymore. That post still hits hard, and it’s a testament to how raw it was. I’m also shocked that it was published just three years ago, although I’m certain it was written years earlier. Reflecting back on things, I realise now that it’s just a date, but it’s a date that is important to me because it’s an anniversary of my choice to live.

item.title: Mini Essay - Before You're 40
item.description:
With just three months away, it’s suddenly becoming a big and urgent question of what you want to do before you’re 40, and more importantly what kind of life you want to live in your 40’s. You never really thought you’d make it to 30, and yet here you are nearly 10 years later wondering what you want to do next.

You 40s really need to be about embracing the life you want to live and reinforcing those things you love most. There’s no question you love writing books on your own, thinking deeply about difficult things, and sharing experiences with others who would never do see what you see without you. Your 40s should be about being bolder in the things you excel at, and cutting free the things that drag. All the philosophy you want to live by is already within you, already hashed out in your notes - now if the time to live it fully.

item.title: Mini Essay - Before You're 50
item.description: For the last few months since I turned 40, I’ve been trying to reassess my life and all the things I’ve done so far with limited success. Much of the challenge has come from knowing just how much there is to sort through and reframe, coupled with having ignored my writing for so long that it feels like there’s a kind of psychic constipation built-up - my recent writing is easing that pressure, but there is a whole lot clogged up that needs to be processed while still more builds up behind it.

item.title: Mini Essay - Choosing between potential jobs
item.description: Right now you’re looking at two different job opportunities, and both of them offer different elements of what you’re looking for in a career in cyber. It’s also important to remember that you don’t need either of these roles - they’re the first to come back to you, and they’ve both provided you with 2nd interviews today, but that doesn’t mean that either of them is the right fit for you - only that they’re the things that are being offered this week.

item.title: Mini Essay - Desires from work and a career in cyber
item.description: To determine what you want from work and your career in cybersecurity more generally, you really need to go back to why you got into cyber in the first place. This whole journey started because you were looking for work that was IT-related, because you haven’t never worked in IT have an aptitude for it. Your initial investigations were leading you down the Gaming pathway - that’s why you spoke to Martin about his work as much as you did, and why you bought a couple of cheap courses in modelling/gaming design in Unity. The interest in working with computers came first, and then the specialisation.

item.title: Mini Essay - Digital Garden
item.description:
First #mini-essay

While the internet has been overwhelmingly consumed with a “feed” or “stream” style where information and opinions are delivered as an unalterable fact, the early days of the internet were far more collaborative and interwoven.

The earliest web pages behaved much like a digital “garden” rather than a feed or chronological blog - posts and snippets of information being woven together in a dense tapestry that was always evolving and interlinking. While a feed provides the most recent and “important” content at the top, a digital garden provides a wide array of entry points and no two journey’s through it are the same. For the last 20 years the internet has evolved into a broad array of feeds all vying for the attention of visitors, delivering the latest and greatest at all times.

item.title: Mini Essay - Drafting my 500 Dives book
item.description: A few months ago I made the decision that I’d write a book about my first 500 cave dives, right around the time I realised I’d be hitting my 500th cave dive during Trip - Sulawesi - 2025 Aug. Since then the ideas associated with this book have rolled around my head, but I’ve not sat down to make a solid go at a draft, and if I’m honest this #mini-essay is potentially another stalling tactic, but at least I’m writing about the idea of this book - it’s a start.

item.title: Mini Essay - Dune
item.description: For years now I’ve felt this overwhelming connection to the Dune universe, and in many ways that connection has felt as undefinable as the series itself. Some might refer to the “vibe” of Dune being appealing, but for me there’s something more than just enjoying the aesthetic - it’s the whole body understanding that if you stop moving, if you try to stay in one place, to put up defences, to block the flow of energy… then you’ll be destroyed and swept away regardless.

item.title: Mini Essay - Emotional Baggage
item.description:
For awhile now I’ve been thinking about the emotional baggage I’m still carrying, and the overwhelming desire to shed it. As far as I can tell, it really centers on two different perceptions: a sense of hurt or harm from the things that happened in the past, and the sense that I’ve invested so much previously and feel drained by the lack of return.

On the “hurt” front, I guess a big part of me still feels broken by 2020, and even by things that happened in 2019. There’s no question that the experience of Georgie’s crash and then the final collapse of Mars One really broke me, but I also know that I’ve recovered from worse. It’s also nearly 6 years since all of that happened - another year and all of the cells in my body will have changed, and I’ll literally be a new person. The bigger issue isn’t the loss or the hurt, it’s that it’s not been replaced with something that was bigger or better. You’ve always sought adventure, and then used the valleys between to develop your stories, but after being involved in something like Mars One a lot of what’ s to come is going to feel like valleys. You will continue to be drawn into extraordinary adventures, and you’ll plan and develop your own adventures too, but there is really too much story inside you right now and it’s making it difficult to enjoy the daily joys. You wrote Cosmic Nomad as a way of letting go of Mars One, and you started your Australian cave diving adventure a year before - now is the time to write the book about your cave diving beginnings and let them go too. You’re ready to level up what you’re doing, and it really feels like you have until ADEX to get all of that sorted - to publish and talk about your Book - Cave Diving at ADEX. Everything else you’re doing is amazing, but the real strength for you is in storytelling about an incredible sport that you love. So let go of that hurt by telling the story of how you got to where you are today.

item.title: Mini Essay - Fear Is The Mind Killer
item.description:
“Fear is the mind killer” is the most easily recognised line from the “Litany Against Fear” from the Dune universe. Recited by high-born characters in times of high stress or when death threatens, it acts to centre and stabilise the emotions of those who recited it through the application of cold logic.

Accepting fear and allowing it to pass over you is vital to remaining in control when it could take control of your mind. In the universe of Dune, the litany is adopted as a vaccine to a digital virus that feeds on fear. However it’s origin can be traced back to Act II of Shakespeare’s Julius Caesar, in a quote which has been adapted numerous times - most notably paraphrased as “A coward dies a thousand deaths, but the brave die only once”.

item.title: Mini Essay - First Day in Ushuaia
item.description: It’s your first day in Ushuaia and you’re naturally shattered from not sleeping in the last 2.5 days, but you’re managing well considering that. You definitely got a good feel for this place though, enough that you certainly reached a point earlier where you were tired, hungry and sore, and the magic of being so close to Antarctica (with the matching weather) had worn off and you just wanted to stop.

item.title: Mini Essay - Frustration at People and Communities
item.description:
Related:

I’m starting to realise that the issues I’ve had with Australian cave divers over the last 5-6 years has a lot of parallels with the way I struggled dealing with people in mining and in the military. Because right now it feels like the Australian cave diving community is bringing out the worst in me much the same way that the Royal Marines brought out the worst in me, and mining nearly drove me to suicide. I know that it’s the schemas that I use to view the world that are creating these parallels, but that doesn’t mean that they impact me any less - it simply means that I can address them by identifying my own thought patterns.
